Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
11:55 PM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying someone as easy as sending a message. You open any payment app, scan a code or type a phone number, enter your PIN, and the money moves from your bank account in seconds. There is no card to carry, no cash to count and no change to hunt for.

It also works almost everywhere. A tea stall, a vegetable seller and a big shop can all take the same QR code payment. Shopkeepers like it because the money lands straight in their bank account, and they don't need an expensive machine. Since it runs 24 hours a day, including holidays, it fits how people actually live and shop.

Here are the three main reasons:

It's free or very cheap. Most people pay nothing to send money to friends or shops, so there is little reason to go back to cards or cash.
It's fast and simple. A payment takes a few seconds, works across different banks and apps, and needs only a phone.
It's everywhere. From small street vendors to online shops and bill payments, nearly everyone accepts it, and even small towns and villages have joined in.

Together, these make UPI the easiest choice for most daily payments.
